extracted.intended_audience: painters, artists, art students, poets and art theorists
extracted.subtask_description: A theoretical and practical guide to painting that sets out what painting must represent and how it should be executed—covering invention, drawing, perspective, proportion, light and shade, subject-matter breadth, and the emotional/ethical aims of the art. Emphasises painting's superiority to poetry in representing visible nature and actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range of painting: surface, colour and shape
rubrics_metrics.description: Painting includes in its range the surface, colour and shape of anything created by nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Painting must capture the visible qualities of natural things (surface, colour, shape). The painter seizes the primary truth of bodies as perceived by the eye, a truth which philosophy notes but does not merely replicate. Aim for fidelity to the eye's perception rather than abstract essences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Movements appropriate to mental attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: If in the painting the movements are appropriate to the mental attributes of the figures...the deaf man will understand the action and intentions of the figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gestures, poses and bodily movement must express the characters' intentions and emotions clearly. Evaluate whether the physical action matches the mental state so that viewers can 'read' intention from posture and movement without verbal explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony of proportion (simultaneous concord)
rubrics_metrics.description: From the concord of many diverse [features] there ensues a well-proportioned harmony which will please the sense of sight...a harmonious concord which delights the eye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose parts so their proportions create an immediate unified harmony analogous to musical concord. Avoid breaking the subject into sequential descriptions; aim for simultaneous, balanced proportion among parts to produce visual harmony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediacy and clarity to the eye
rubrics_metrics.description: Painting reveals itself immediately to thee with the semblance given it by its creator, and affords to the chief of the senses as great a delight as any object created by nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A painting should convey its essence at a glance and require minimal commentary. Strive for clarity so the viewer perceives subject, action and beauty instantly rather than relying on explanatory text or prolonged interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durability and preservation of depicted beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Time in a few years destroys [living beauty], but this does not occur in the case of beauty depicted by the painter, because time preserves it for long.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques and materials that preserve colour and form (e.g., enamel on copper) are valued; consider permanence when aiming to immortalize a subject. Durability is an aesthetic and cultural virtue of painting compared with ephemeral arts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention and measure (subject invention and proportional measure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet says that his science consists of invention and rhythm...the painter re-joins that he is governed by the same necessities...invention and measure (fancy as regards the subject matter which he must invent, and measure as regards the matters painted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Painting requires both imaginative invention of subjects and precise measurement/proportion in execution. Develop original subject matter while ensuring measured, proportionate depiction of forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of drawing and perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: First strive in drawing to express to the eye in a manifest shape the idea and the fancy originally devised by thy imagination...as regards dimension and size, in accordance with perspective there is no portion of the work which is not in harmony with reason and natural effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with strong drawing that communicates the concept. Use models (clothed or nude) and rigorous perspective so every element respects spatial dimensions and natural appearances. Perspective is the principal technical foundation and must be accurate across the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth of subject-matter and versatility
rubrics_metrics.description: Painting embraces in itself all the forms of nature...he seems to me to be a poor master who can only do one thing well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good painter should be able to depict people, animals, plants, landscapes, buildings, costumes, instruments, and varied effects—not be narrowly specialized. Strive for competence across many natural forms and settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of light, shade, colour and atmospheric effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The painter places the light and shade...the painter can give the idea of a distance of a hundred miles beyond the picture...can represent transparent bodies, reflections, nor bodies as lustrous as mirrors, and other translucent objects, neither mists nor dark skies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop techniques for chiaroscuro, colour handling, reflections, translucency, and aerial perspective to depict textures and atmospheric depth. These capabilities distinguish painting from sculpture and are essential to convincing representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional and persuasive impact
rubrics_metrics.description: By painting lovers are attracted to the images of the beloved...he will most certainly be struck dizzy with admiration and incomparable joy...Write the name of God in some spot, and set up His image opposite, and you will see which will be the most reverenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for works that move viewers—incite love, wonder, reverence or moral understanding. Evaluate whether the image achieves a stronger emotional or devotional response than verbal description could.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show rather than tell: pictorial economy over verbal prolixity
rubrics_metrics.description: Painting is mute poetry, and poetry is blind painting...it is a sin against nature to attempt to transmit by the ear that which should be transmitted by the eye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer visual demonstration to lengthy verbal description. Avoid trying to make a painting do the job of prose; let the image communicate what words would otherwise laboriously describe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous wholeness: whole visible at once
rubrics_metrics.description: The painter shows the whole at the same time...the poet in describing the beauty or the ugliness of any body reveals it to you limb by limb and at diverse times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose scenes so that the viewer apprehends the whole composition and the relations between parts simultaneously. Avoid fragmentary presentation that forces the eye to assemble the image over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of models and incremental correction
rubrics_metrics.description: First strive in drawing...then go on adding or removing until thou art satisfied; then arrange men as models, clothed or nude...acting on sound rules, he will remove so little at a time that his work will be brought to a successful close.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work iteratively: sketch, adjust gradually, use live models appropriately clothed or nude according to intent. Make small corrections rather than large destructive changes; consistent, careful refinement leads to better results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Painting as a learned, mathematical art
rubrics_metrics.description: Perspective...the principal link of painting...she has given symbols to the mathematicians; she has taught geometry its figures, and instructed the astrologers, the makers of machines and engineers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach painting with intellectual discipline: geometry, mathematics and perspective inform composition and proportion. Treat technical foundations as scholarly subjects to be mastered, not merely manual tricks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical aim: honour over mercenary motives
rubrics_metrics.description: O painter, beware lest in thee the lust of gain should overcome the honour of thy art, for the acquisition of honour is a much greater thing than the glory of wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise artistic honour and the integrity of the work over profit. Beware of letting financial motives degrade artistic standards or lead to narrow specialization for money's sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to invent and compose imaginary subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: If the painter wishes to see beautiful things which will enchant him he is able to beget them; if he wishes to see monstrous things...he can dispose of all these...all quantities of things that exist in the universe, either real or imaginary, he has first in his mind and then in his hands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate imaginative power to conceive scenes and creatures not present in nature and to compose them convincingly. Use invention responsibly to create coherent, believable images that still obey pictorial rules of proportion and light.
